reason: The cited evidence supports that CTE mismatch causes cracking (E4) and that Al2O3 is protective (E1, E3), but no cited passage provides data on lattice matching between specific oxides and CrFeCoNiX substrates, nor on how grain boundaries mediate stress relaxation in these alloys. The claim that Si or Mn oxides have greater mismatch is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Selective oxidation of X forms a protective oxide whose crystallography and thermal expansion match the substrate
Lattice match (low mismatch) between oxide and alloy determines interface coherency and adherence
Grain boundary density and character mediate oxygen diffusion and stress relaxation in the oxide scale
Oxide growth kinetics influence microcrack formation and spallation
Al forms α-Al2O3 with good lattice matching, while Si or Mn oxides have greater mismatch
